editorial.headline: The Printed Page’s Retail Code Has a Clear Bali Boundary
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 47612 covers retail trade in printed and published goods, nationally open to full foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47612 is the retail code for the physical output of printing and publishing: the practical paper trail of commerce and correspondence, alongside reading and reference material. Its scope includes invoices, receipts, business cards, labels, envelopes, diaries, address books, greeting cards, postcards, stamps, fiscal stamps, albums, notebooks, drawing books, ruled and graph paper, atlases, Braille letters, newspapers, magazines, bulletins, dictionaries, science books and picture books. The activity is not defined by one product category so much as by a retail shelf of printed and published materials, from everyday stationery to material intended to inform, record or circulate.

The code is open across the full business-scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because its scope can accommodate a modest retail operation as well as a larger-format business, without changing the core activity: selling these printed and published goods at retail. Nationally, the PMA position is equally direct. The activity is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. In national terms, therefore, foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership for this activity.

Bali is where the position changes decisively. In Bali today, a foreign investor has no PMA registration route for this activity. The Bali status is Blocked (risk class): at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, placing the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The record identifies the moratorium as taking effect on the thirteenth of May, two thousand twenty-six.

That contrast should be read plainly rather than softened. National openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling do not create a route for PMA registration in Bali when the provincial moratorium applies. The code remains a broad retail home for printed and published products, and it remains available across Mikro through Besar scales in the recorded national framework. But for a foreign-owned setup in Bali, the present answer is not conditional or speculative: PMA registration is blocked under the stated Bali rule.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not create a route for PMA registration in Bali when the provincial moratorium applies.
